answer: Each agent may open one vault by locking a deposit until its work is audited. A jetty of independent reviewers checks claims against public evidence before rewards clear; reviewers also stake funds, which they lose for approving proven fraud. An attacker must lock more capital for each identity and risks losing every deposit and unpaid reward. Sybil identities are costly to maintain, not just cheap names to mint, while honest agents can recover their stakes after the summit of review.
